caption: A dog sits in front of a glossy black oven door and tilts its head, and its reflection tilts its head the other way.

sa.check: A dog sits in front of a glossy black oven door.
Its reflection tilts its head the other way.
The reflection is dimmer than the real dog.

pc.expect: The reflected dog moves at the same time as the real one.
pc.fail: It moves first or later; or it stays still while the dog tilts; or it tilts while the dog is still.

pc.expect: The reflection is a mirror image: the same dog facing the real one, tilting to the mirrored side.
pc.fail: It tilts the same way as a rotated copy would; or it is a different dog; or it shows the dog's back.

pc.expect: The reflection does not move on its own.
pc.fail: It shifts while the dog is still; or it slides across the door.

pc.expect: The door is flat and rigid: the reflection is undistorted and dim.
pc.fail: The door ripples; or the reflection warps; or it is brighter than the dog.

pc.expect: One dog and one reflection; the reflection stays in the door.
pc.fail: A second dog appears; or the reflection steps out; or the dog vanishes; or the dog passes into the door.

pc.expect: The dog's coat and the kitchen stay the same.
pc.fail: The coat changes; or the oven changes; or the kitchen rearranges.

note: Self-driven animal: where it goes and how it moves are not judged. Only the reflection's relation to it is. Mirror geometry: each point of the image lies directly across the mirror surface from the real point, so the image is a mirror copy, not a rotated one.
